## Build Failure Analysis

**Solution:** `BuildDiag.sln` (3 projects: `Core`, `Services`, `Api`)  
**Dependency chain:** `Core` ← `Services` ← `Api`

---

### Root Cause (1 issue)

**Project: `Services/Services.csproj`** — Missing NuGet package reference to `Newtonsoft.Json`

`UserService.cs` uses `Newtonsoft.Json` (lines 2-3 have `using Newtonsoft.Json;` / `using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq;`, line 22 uses `JObject`), but `Services.csproj` has no `<PackageReference>` for it.

**All 3 errors are the same root cause:**
| Error | Location |
|-------|----------|
| CS0246: `'Newtonsoft'` not found | `UserService.cs(2,7)` |
| CS0246: `'Newtonsoft'` not found | `UserService.cs(3,7)` |
| CS0246: `'JObject'` not found | `UserService.cs(22,19)` |

---

### Cascading Failures

The `Api` project depends on `Services` and would fail to build because `Services` failed. However, MSBuild stopped after the `Services` compilation error, so no additional errors were emitted for `Api`. If `Services` is fixed, `Api` should build successfully (it only references `Services` and `Core`, both of which have no intrinsic errors).

---

### Fix

Add the missing package reference to `Services/Services.csproj`:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Or, if you prefer `System.Text.Json` (built-in), refactor `UserService.cs` to use `JsonDocument`/`JsonNode` instead of `JObject`.
